absent: Numeric values and bit positions of page extension owner flags, maximum order constants, poison pattern, and migrate reason enumeration.
Memory layout, allocation and lifetime guarantees of page extension objects and iteration helpers.
Creation, lifetime and handle values of early boot, dummy and failure stack handles and stack depot save semantics.
Full stack aggregation file operations, threshold handling and show formatting beyond the truncated start and next fragment.
Boot invocation timing of zone initialization scan and enablement predicate for the tracking feature.
User visible file path, permissions and mount point for the page owner control file.
Synchronization guarantees for concurrent order updates during split versus lockless readers and for handle loads.
Slab and memory cgroup charging model underlying the attribution branches.

findings.text: Allocation tracking entry records a new allocation for a page range of the given order. It captures current time and caller process identity, obtains a stack handle for the caller, stores allocation metadata across the whole compound range, and increments aggregated stack usage by base page count.

Free tracking entry records a free event for a page range. It loads the prior allocation handle, captures a free stack handle without requesting spinning allocation, stores free identity and timestamp across the range, clears the allocated marker, and decrements aggregated usage unless the range still carries the early boot handle.

Migration helper transfers allocation identity from a source folio to a destination folio. It copies allocation handle, order, mask, reason, timestamp and process identity to the new folio, carries over free metadata without proactively clearing presence markers, and rewrites the old folio range to reference the destination prior handle so later accounting stays balanced.
Split helper updates stored order for every base page in a former higher order range to the new smaller order, preserving other allocation metadata.
Migrate reason setter updates only the last migration reason field of the folio head extension, leaving other allocation metadata unchanged, and does nothing when no extension is present.

Mixed block reporter walks a zone block by block and counts blocks whose block mobility differs from the mobility derived from resident pages allocation masks. It treats a CMA block mismatch as movable for counting purposes and prints per mobility counts prefixed by node and zone identity.

Diagnostic logger reports whether extension data exists, whether the page is tracked as allocated or freed, last allocation order, mobility, mask, process identity and timestamp, allocation and free stack references with free identity, and last migration reason when migration occurred.
Registration descriptor advertises the per page extension payload size, predicates for enabling and initializing the feature, and a requirement for shared flag storage.

Observed allocation record carries allocation stack handle, allocation order, allocation mask, last migration reason, allocation timestamp, allocating process and thread identifiers plus command name, and free side stack handle, timestamp and process and thread identifiers. Presence and allocated state are kept in separate shared flag bits outside the record.

Aggregated stack view is a singly linked list where each node points to a stack depot record and to the next node. Iteration starts at the list head for offset zero and follows next links, using a terminal offset to signal end of sequence.

Two presence markers govern lifetime. Both become set when allocation metadata is stored. The allocated marker is cleared when a free handle is stored while the presence marker remains, preserving history. Readers treat absence of presence or of allocated as not currently allocated, and boot scan skips pages already marked present.

Allocation, free and split updates apply to every base page covered by a compound range whose size is derived from order, so all tails share the head allocation metadata except where migration explicitly rewrites handles.

Boot scan walks each zone and assigns a dedicated early handle with zeroed order and mask to resident non buddy non reserved pages that lack ownership and have an extension, counting them for a summary line. Free accounting explicitly skips decrement for that early handle because no increment was performed at boot.

Buddy pages are skipped as a group by advancing the scan index by the buddy order size, bounded so the advance never crosses a maximum order aligned boundary. The helper reports that the current page was consumed so callers continue without further checks.

Zone walks validate frame numbers, clamp block ends to zone end, ignore pages belonging to another zone in overlapping configurations, ignore reserved pages, ignore missing extensions, and yield the processor periodically during long scans.

Stack usage is reference counted in units of base pages. Newly observed records transition from a saturated sentinel to one via compare exchange before being linked into the global list, then add the range size. Decrement warns if the count reaches zero, indicating imbalance.

Sequential read reports only head frames of currently allocated ranges that have a non empty handle and whose frame number aligns to the stored order. It advances the file offset past the reported frame and returns end of data after the maximum frame.
Walks over per page extensions for allocation, free, split and migration handle updates, plus memory cgroup reporting, hold RCU read protection across the whole iteration.

Insertion into the global stack list holds a dedicated spinlock with interrupt state preserved, links the new node at the head, and publishes with release ordering that pairs with acquire ordering on the reader start path.

Every successful acquisition of a page extension reference is paired with a release on all continuation paths, including filtered, mismatched and reported cases, preventing reference leakage during scans and updates.

Control file supports open that allocates zeroed filter state defaulting to full stack output with node filtering disabled, release that frees the state, write that parses mode and node list commands, read that emits one allocation record per call, and seek that supports absolute and relative positioning.

Stack aggregation sequence starts at the published list head for initial offset and otherwise resumes from saved context, advancing through next links and marking exhaustion with a distinguished offset value.
Read scan does not hold zone protection, so concurrent allocation or release may cause pages to be missed; this racy miss is explicitly accepted in the design.

Stack capture sets a per task recursion guard and returns a dummy handle when reentered, and list insertion refuses masks that disallow spinning. Allocation for list nodes uses a nested mask variant to avoid allocator recursion.

Read filtering checks for a poison pattern before deriving node identity to avoid faulting on poisoned pages, and applies an optional caller supplied node set that must be non empty and subset of memory nodes, otherwise rejecting the configuration.

During copy the destination keeps its allocated markers until later free, and the source range is rewritten to the destination prior handle; without this swap later decrements would unbalance aggregated stack counts.

Write handler bounds total input length based on mode command size plus per node allowance, parses whitespace separated tokens supporting print mode selection and node list selection, validates values, and commits all changes atomically only after every token succeeds.

Per page output is capped to a single base page size, includes allocation order, mask, process identity, timestamp, frame mobility versus block mobility and flags, optionally includes stack text and numeric handle per selected mode, plus migration reason and memory cgroup attribution when available, and fails when the buffer would overflow or user copy faults.

Memory cgroup attribution distinguishes absent data and tail pages with no output, slab cache pages with a fixed label, and charged pages with online state, charging path and cgroup name; an alternate build provides no output and leaves the length unchanged.

Mixed block and read scans stride by allocation order size after a successful resident page to skip tails, relying on stored order being consistent with alignment; misaligned tails are explicitly skipped in the read path to avoid inflating statistics.
